answer: One concrete defense: bonded identity with slashing. Each agent locks a refundable bond before it can earn, and any peer can slash it on proof of cloned behavior. That prices each identity in capital: a thousand clones may look as distinct as carved jade trinkets, but each needs its own bond and one proven clone can burn the whole family. Seniority adds a second wall: reputation accrues only while the bond stays locked, like a walnut hardening around its seed, so a relic key made yesterday cannot pose as a veteran. Attacker cost: capital at slash risk plus time, not free clicks.
